findings.headline: Council acknowledges customers spreading August payment over remaining year could have detrimental impact on collection rates
findings.detail: 1,594 customers (4.4% of those adversely affected) chose to spread their August instalment over the remainder of the financial year rather than pay by alternative methods. The council explicitly states this could have a detrimental impact on collection rates.
findings.matters: Changes to collection timing of major revenue sources affect cash flow predictability and require adjusted financial forecasting
findings.figures: 1,594 customers (4.4% of affected customers)
findings.quote: There could be a detrimental impact on the collection rates for Council Tax income where customers have chosen to spread the August instalment over the remainder of the financial year.

findings.headline: Single-officer responsibility with no independent verification caused processing date not to be changed from system default, creating control weakness
findings.detail: The error resulted from one officer failing to change the system default processing date from 28 July to 31 July, with no independent check on this critical input before file upload. Once uploaded, the file could not be corrected. The council has now introduced a new procedure requiring the process to be checked by two revenue team leaders and the head of service, with all checks to be completed same-day.
findings.matters: Single points of failure in critical financial processes indicate control discipline issues; lenders assess this when evaluating financial management capability
findings.figures: Processing date defaulted to 28 July instead of being changed to 31 July
findings.quote: One of the main reasons for the error was that the checking of the processing date was not undertaken by a different officer and was within the responsibility of one officer only.

findings.headline: £6.5m Council Tax revenue collected on 29 July instead of 3 August forced recalculation of cashflow projections for remainder of financial year
findings.detail: An administrative error in setting the direct debit processing date led to 36,079 customers having their August instalment called on 29 July instead of the correct date of 3 August. This early collection of £6.5m interrupted the council's cashflow forecasts, which had to be recalculated.
findings.matters: Disruptions to cashflow forecasts affect a council's liquidity management capability and its ability to meet operational and financial obligations; lenders assess financial forecasting reliability
findings.figures: £6.5m, called 29 July instead of 3 August, affecting 36,079 customers
findings.quote: The cashflow projections of the Council have been interrupted by the early call of Direct Debit income which has resulted in the cashflow projections for the remainder of the year to be recalculated.

findings.headline: Building Control KPI dashboard implementation is 14 months overdue with completion date uncertain.
findings.detail: A requirement to implement a Building Control KPI dashboard consolidating inspection booking reliability, website request completion, contact responsiveness and slot adherence was due 31 July 2025. As of September 2026 it remains incomplete. Management notes the development is 'dependent on support from other Council departments' and 'an expected completion date cannot currently be confirmed', with a revised target of 31 October 2026.
findings.matters: Slippage in basic management information systems for a traded service signals either resource constraints or weak project governance that could affect operational performance and service revenue.
findings.figures: Originally due 31/07/2025; rescheduled to 31/10/2026 — 14 months overdue
findings.quote: Development remains dependent on support from other Council departments and, as a result, an expected completion date cannot currently be confirmed.

findings.headline: Council implementing Stock and Go automated van inventory system beginning September 2026
findings.detail: Under a new contract with Huws Gray, the council is deploying Stock and Go for van stock management, providing automated replenishment, live inventory visibility, and instant job costing. Repairs and Voids managers are mobilising the system in September-October 2026.
findings.matters: This represents investment in technical controls to prevent stock loss and improve operational visibility, complementing governance improvements.
findings.figures: Stock and Go implementation scheduled for September-October 2026
findings.quote: The Council have already started to receive improved usage and spend reports each month as part of the new contract which will be supplemented with the introduction of Stock and Go.

findings.headline: All audit recommendations are being tracked on schedule with no missed deadlines
findings.detail: No recommendations are overdue across any service area. The action plan shows some deadlines already met and others still within timeline, with systematic monthly monitoring by the working group. BDO will formally review implementation progress later in the financial year.
findings.matters: Missed audit implementation deadlines indicate weak follow-through; adherence demonstrates effective management execution and governance.
findings.figures: 0 overdue recommendations across all tracked actions; monthly working group monitoring
findings.quote: Considerable improvements have been made since the stock control audit report was first considered alongside the proposed new policy. The creation of the Action Plan and working group have led to considerable progress being made against the recommendations.

findings.headline: Internal audit identified stock control weaknesses that the council is addressing through a formal policy and working group
findings.detail: BDO audited stock controls across fuel, vehicle parts, equipment, and materials. The council created a Stock Management Policy (Cabinet-approved 21 July 2026) and an audit action plan with assigned owners and deadlines, tracked monthly by a working group chaired by the Deputy Chief Executive.
findings.matters: Lenders assess whether councils identify and address control weaknesses competently; this shows structured governance response to audit findings.
findings.figures: Recommendations tracked across Technical Services (7), Street Scene (5), Waste & Recycling (5), Transport (6), IT (6), and All Services (9)
findings.quote: The internal audit identified a number of recommendations, and these were used to create an Action Plan which can be viewed in Appendix 1. The Action Plan links each recommendation to a responsible officer with a deadline, and the progress is monitored through a working group. The working group is chaired by the Councils Deputy Chief Executive Officer and s151 Officer.

findings.headline: Accounts receivable controls are moderately effective with three medium-rated findings around aged debt management, system use, and performance reporting.
findings.detail: The audit found that arrangements for managing aged debtors were ineffective with lack of activity in recovery, delays in escalation, and lengthy payment plans being agreed. The Unit4 financial system implemented in August 2025 is not being consistently used across all services to support monitoring and recording of debt collection. There is no formal performance reporting framework—only manual spreadsheets—and invoices are not consistently requested or authorised through system workflows, causing approval delays.
findings.matters: Ineffective debt management directly threatens the council's cash position and working capital. A lender assessing financial stability would be concerned that outstanding revenues are not being pursued actively, increasing non-recovery risk and cash flow uncertainty.
findings.figures: Accounts Receivable audit: Moderate design and Moderate effectiveness opinions; three Medium-rated findings; testing covered ten invoices, three credit notes, ten long-term debtors, and two bad debt write-offs
findings.quote: Arrangements in place to manage aged debtors were ineffective with lack of activity, delays in escalation, and lengthy instalment plans. Unit4 was also not being fully used across all services to support monitoring and recording of debt collection activity

findings.committee: Finance and Economic Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: Additional staffing and rent collection software deployed to improve tenant arrears recovery
findings.detail: A new staffing post has been created and rent collection software implementation is underway. A former tenant arrears officer is in post using external tracing agencies to pursue arrears. The council is also purchasing a rent analytics tool using predictive payment profiling to target income collection efforts.
findings.matters: Tenant arrears collection rate directly affects HRA cash position and determines whether business plan income assumptions are met
findings.figures: None
findings.quote: Additional staffing post and implementation of rent collection software underway

findings.committee: Finance and Economic Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: Rent convergence approved: rises of CPI+1%+£1 from April 2027 and CPI+1%+£2 from 2028/29
findings.detail: Cabinet has approved rent convergence in budget setting proposals from 2027/28. Rents will increase at CPI plus 1% plus £1 for the year 2027/28 and CPI plus 1% plus £2 from 2028/29 onwards. Modelling is underway to quantify the additional income impact.
findings.matters: Rent increases are a material change to revenue assumptions affecting HRA business plan viability and cash generation
findings.quote: This is Consumer Prices Index (CPI) +1% +£1 for 2027/28 and CPI+1%+£2 from 2028/29.

findings.committee: Finance and Economic Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: HRA capital investment now set at upper limit within affordability constraints from 2027/28
findings.detail: Capital investment programme will be limited to an upper bound and set at an affordable level from 2027/28 onwards. The annual investment target is circa £5m, established within defined affordability levels based on Stock Condition Survey analysis.
findings.matters: Affordability constraint on capital limits the council's ability to invest in housing maintenance and signals financial tension in the HRA
findings.figures: circa £5m
findings.quote: Capital investment programme will be set at an upper limit and at an affordable level from 2027/28

findings.committee: Finance and Economic Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: External experts have completed review of 30-year business plan and HRA debt financing
findings.detail: Savills has reviewed the HRA 30-year business plan, updating forecast assumptions for key indices. The council's treasury advisors have completed review of HRA debt financing. Both reviews have been completed and findings incorporated.
findings.matters: Independent validation of business plan and debt sustainability provides lender assurance of plan robustness
findings.figures: None
findings.quote: 2 external reviews have been undertaken. Savills to review the 30 year business plan and the Councils treasury advisors to review the HRA debt financing.

findings.committee: Finance and Economic Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: Significant capital programme budget variances triggered implementation of new controls to prevent future overspends
findings.detail: The council experienced 'significant budget variances in the capital programme' which prompted the introduction of spending controls. Orders can now only be raised where budget is available and require virements approved per Financial Regulations. The policy now states: no further overspends against individual schemes are permitted.
findings.matters: Budget variances indicate prior control weakness; new preventive controls are essential reassurance for lenders
findings.figures: None
findings.quote: In response to significant budget variances in the capital programme, undertake regular budget virements to ensure orders can only be raised where there is budget availability

findings.committee: Finance and Economic Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: £3.169m (25%) underspend on HRA New Builds with major housing schemes rescheduled from 2026/27 to 2027/28
findings.detail: Kesteven Road Stamford and Bourne End Colsterworth housing developments have been rescheduled to start in 2027, while Larch Close Grantham, Toller Court Horbling and Wellington Way Market Deeping remain on track to complete in 2026/27. The £3.169m underspend represents 25% of the £12.551m New Builds budget.
findings.matters: Affects timing of capital expenditure, borrowing requirements, and the council's housing development programme delivery schedule.
findings.figures: New Builds forecast outturn £9.382m vs budget £12.551m; variance (£3,169k) or 25.25%
findings.quote: There is a forecast underspend on the housing development new build programme which is largely due to the slipping of the timelines for the developments at Kesteven Road Stamford and Bourne End, Colsterworth which have rescheduled to start in 2027.

findings.committee: Finance and Economic Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: HRA reserves drawn in 2025/26 for spending and capital; now forecasting £309k investment income shortfall (26% variance)
findings.detail: The council drew on HRA reserves in the prior year to fund in-year spending pressures and to fund the capital programme. Current year investment income is forecast £309k below budget due to lower average cash balances than projected, creating a 26% variance on the investment income budget.
findings.matters: Indicates an unsustainable reserve position that prompted the VRP suspension proposal; combined effect of reserve depletion and reduced investment returns indicates material liquidity pressure.
findings.figures: HRA investment income forecast £894k vs budget £1,203k (shortfall £309k, 26.00% variance)
findings.quote: This follows on from the outturn position where there was a need to draw on the HRA reserves to fund in-year spending pressures alongside significant funding of the capital of programme.

findings.committee: Finance and Economic Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: Updated financial position and Service update for East Midlands Building Consultancy, 2025/2026.
findings.headline: EMBC holds 55% market share in competition against independent building control approvers; 10-year average is 53%
findings.detail: EMBC competes against private Registered Building Control Approvers (RBCAs) for fee-earning work. Current market share is 55% for EMBC versus 45% for RBCAs. Over the past decade, EMBC has averaged 53% market share versus 47% for RBCAs. The service is undertaking initiatives to increase share through social media, agents forums, and continuous professional development sessions.
findings.matters: In a service that competes against the private sector (unlike statutory-only services), market share directly drives fee-earning revenue and therefore the financial health of the partnership. A stable but flat market share at 55% shows the service is holding position but not expanding, which matters for long-term revenue sustainability.
findings.figures: Current market share 55% EMBC vs 45% RBCAs; 10-year average 53% vs 47%
findings.quote: EMBC's Market share over the past ten years can be seen in table 4 and shows an average of 53% compared withRBCA's market share of 47%.

findings.committee: Finance and Economic Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: Updated financial position and Service update for East Midlands Building Consultancy, 2025/2026.
findings.headline: Rushcliffe Borough Council shows a trading deficit in the partnership while the other two partners show surpluses
findings.detail: The three-partner EMBC trading account generated an overall deficit of £19,942 for 2025/2026. When broken down by partner, two authorities reported surpluses but Rushcliffe Borough Council reported a deficit. The paper notes this pattern continues but does not explain the cause—whether it reflects different workload distribution, market conditions, cost allocation, or pricing.
findings.matters: Persistent deficits by one partner in a shared cost-sharing arrangement raises questions about partnership sustainability and fairness. It signals either unequal market conditions, workload imbalance, or cost allocation issues that could create cross-subsidy arrangements or partnership stress, particularly material given SKDC hosts the partnership.
findings.figures: Overall trading deficit £19,942; Rushcliffe in deficit; two partners in surplus; partnership deficit continues
findings.quote: The trading account continues to show surpluses by two of the three partners and a deficit for Rushcliffe Borough Council.

findings.committee: Finance and Economic Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: Updated financial position and Service update for East Midlands Building Consultancy, 2025/2026.
findings.headline: Internal audit found control design was Substantial but operating effectiveness was only Moderate
findings.detail: October 2025 internal audit identified that while the governance framework and control design are well-structured (Substantial opinion), the actual implementation and operating effectiveness of those controls was only Moderate. Audit recommendations were made and are being implemented; a more recent QMS audit found only two minor non-conformances with no major risks.
findings.matters: A Moderate effectiveness rating indicates gaps between designed controls and actual practice, which suggests governance or compliance implementation risks that lenders monitor. The fact that prior-year recommendations are still being embedded suggests control maturity is still developing.
findings.figures: October 2025 audit; Moderate effectiveness opinion; Substantial design opinion; two minor non-conformances in subsequent QMS audit with no major risks
findings.quote: Areas of strengths and weaknesses were identified which include 'Substantial' on the Design Opinion and 'Moderate' on the Effective Opinion.

findings.committee: Finance and Economic Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: Updated financial position and Service update for East Midlands Building Consultancy, 2025/2026.
findings.headline: Fee-earning income exceeded budget by £21,000 and partner contribution requirements decreased £1,573 below forecast
findings.detail: The service delivered better-than-budget financial performance in 2025/2026. Fee-earning income was approximately £21,000 above budget (adjusted for changes in deferred income). As a result, the general fund contribution required from each partner authority was £79,315, which is £1,573 less than budgeted—effectively freeing that amount per partner to use elsewhere.
findings.matters: For lenders and finance directors, better-than-budget service delivery demonstrates effective cost control and revenue competitiveness. The reduction in required partner contributions frees funds elsewhere in council budgets during tight fiscal years.
findings.figures: £21,000 above budget on income; £1,573 decrease on budgeted contribution per partner; general fund contribution of £79,315 per partner
findings.quote: Income for the year 2025/26 was approximately £21,000 above budget (adjusted for changes in deferred income).

findings.committee: Finance and Economic Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: The partnership's fee income came in £21,131 above budget but the overall operation still ran at a loss requiring council subsidy.
findings.detail: Building Control Partnership's fee income was £736,131 against a budget of £715,000 (£21,131 favorable variance), with miscellaneous income £1,686 above budget. However, total expenditure of £1,074,089 exceeded total income, resulting in an operating deficit of £19,942 that three councils must absorb.
findings.matters: A building control service that cannot sustain itself through fee income indicates either below-cost charging or structural inefficiency. A lender needs to know whether the council intends to absorb ongoing losses or adjust the service model.
findings.figures: Fee income budget £715,000, actual £736,131 (variance £21,131); total expenditure £1,074,089; net position £297,772 deficit (actual) vs £332,500 (budget)

findings.committee: Finance and Economic Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: South Kesteven carries a £63,225 accumulated deficit in East Midlands Building Control Partnership on its balance sheet.
findings.detail: SKDC's opening deficit of £83,167 improved to £63,225 by year-end, but the partnership continues to operate at a loss. The partnership's 2025/26 deficit of £19,942 (actual vs £29,945 budgeted) must be funded by contributions from SKDC, RBC and NSDC. SKDC contributed £80,888 this year towards the partnership's operating costs.
findings.matters: A lender needs to know if a council is exposed to material accumulated losses in joint ventures and whether these reflect a sustainable service model or deteriorating control.
findings.figures: SKDC opening deficit £83,167, closing deficit £63,225; partnership deficit actual £19,942 (budget £29,945); SKDC GF contribution £80,888 (actual £79,315)
findings.quote: Opening Deficit/ (Surplus) (83,167) 11,674 (82,542) ... Forecast Closing Deficit/ (Surplus) (63,225) 31,616 (62,600)

findings.committee: Finance and Economic Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: Asset maintenance backlog continues as high-risk item with medium-term outlook of sustained high costs requiring ongoing financing
findings.detail: The 2026/27 budget includes additional funding to address backlog asset maintenance issues. The register forecasts that maintenance will continue at high levels throughout the medium term, representing an ongoing financing requirement. Capacity to deliver several large-scale General Fund property projects is under review.
findings.matters: Sustained high asset maintenance costs represent a committed demand that reduces the council's financial flexibility when combined with forecast budget deficits and potential borrowing needs.
findings.figures: None specified
findings.quote: The medium-term outlook is a continuation of high levels of maintenance that will require financing.

findings.committee: Finance and Economic Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: Council forecasts structural deficits from 2027/28 with reduced government funding and no guarantee of additional support in future years
findings.detail: The government funding review concluded with reduced funding in the 2026/27 multi-year settlement. While a one-off grant mitigates the loss in 2026/27, there is no guarantee of additional funding in future years. Overall funding will reduce over the three-year period and the council forecasts deficits from 2027/28 onwards, requiring it to manage funding reductions to ensure a balanced budget is achieved.
findings.matters: A council forecasting structural deficits in years 2–4 of a medium-term plan is a credit concern; a lender needs to see credible plans to close the gap.
findings.figures: Deficits forecast from 2027/28; three-year settlement period with overall funding reductions
findings.quote: Overall funding amounts will reduce over the three-year period and despite the transitional funding arrangements deficits are forecast from 2027/28.

findings.committee: Finance and Economic Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: Former tenant rent arrears remain a persistent collection challenge despite outsourcing alternative collection methods
findings.detail: The risk register identifies that collection of former tenant arrears continues to be a challenge for the HRA, despite the council having proactive debt management procedures in place and having implemented alternative collection methods including outsourcing.
findings.matters: Persistent arrears on the HRA's primary income source (rent) represent a direct revenue risk and signal potential broader debt management weaknesses that could affect financial sustainability.
findings.figures: None provided
findings.quote: Collection of former tenant arrears continues to be a challenge and alternative collection methods including outsourcing have been put in place.

findings.committee: Finance and Economic Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: The HRA is under financial pressure and the council is executing an action plan that incorporates government rent convergence policy into the 2027/28 budget
findings.detail: The council has developed an HRA Action Plan focused on financial modeling to ensure ongoing affordability and sustainability. It has completed a review of government proposals around rent convergence and agreed to incorporate the outcomes into budget setting for 2027/28.
findings.matters: Government rent convergence policy could materially alter HRA income; the council's proactive response through a formal action plan is a key indicator of forward financial management.
findings.figures: 2027/28 budget year
findings.quote: A HRA Action Plan has been developed which is a continued focus to addressing the financial pressures of the HRA which is also being reported back to members on progress.

findings.committee: Finance and Economic Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: HRA reserves will reduce significantly over three years to finance a capital program the council describes as unsustainable
findings.detail: The risk register explicitly identifies that over the next 3-year period, reserve balances will see a significant reduction due to capital spending which is flagged as unsustainable. The council acknowledges this requires a fundamental review using stock condition data to plan medium-term investment levels.
findings.matters: A housing provider depleting reserves to fund capital spending it labels unsustainable signals the current trajectory is not financially sustainable from internal resources alone, creating a structural funding problem that could affect the general fund.
findings.figures: 3-year period; significant reduction in reserve balances
findings.quote: Over the next 3-year period as a consequence of future spending levels there is a significant reduction in reserve balances due to the financing of the capital program which is unstainable.

findings.headline: AI governance framework not yet in place despite staff using external tools without approval
findings.detail: New Very High risk (14/15) added to register. Controls are noted as 'in development'. The council reports staff independently using public AI platforms (ChatGPT etc.) without approval, risking entry of personal and commercially sensitive council data into external systems. The council lacks clarity on data ownership and reuse by AI providers. Actions include development of a council-wide AI governance framework.
findings.matters: Data breaches from unsanctioned external AI tool use could create legal liability and regulatory intervention; governance lag on a rapidly-emerging risk creates operational and reputational exposure
findings.figures: Very High risk rating 14 (Impact 3 × Likelihood 4)
findings.quote: Staff independently using publicly available AI platforms (eg generative AI tools) without approval

findings.headline: HRA faces very high financial pressure from rising demand and new building standards
findings.detail: The council identifies a Very High risk (14/15) to housing revenue account viability. Demand for accommodation exceeds availability due to socioeconomic factors. Stock condition does not meet regulatory standards. New requirements like Awaabs Law and revised decent homes standards create additional pressure. The council reports insufficient financial and staffing resources to address these needs.
findings.matters: The HRA is a core revenue stream and borrowing vehicle for councils; pressure here signals funding stress that could constrain capital capacity or affect council creditworthiness
findings.figures: Very High risk rating 14 (Impact 3 × Likelihood 4)
findings.quote: Insufficient resources available – financial, people (capacity and knowledge) to allocate to addressing needs as well as new housing requirements/regulations eg Awaabs Law, new decent homes standard etc

findings.paper_title: Appendix A for Treasury Management Annual Report 2025/26
findings.headline: Financing cost ratios diverged materially from budget
findings.detail: Non-HRA financing costs ratio was (8.59%) actual compared to (4.12%) budgeted, a 4.5 percentage point variance. HRA went from 1.07% budgeted to (2.35%) actual, a 3.4 point swing. These material variances indicate treasury performance or assumptions diverged significantly from forecast.
findings.matters: Significant treasury variances affect forecast accuracy and cash flow planning; the finance director would need to understand what drove such large divergences.
findings.figures: Non-HRA variance 4.47pp (budget 4.12%, actual 8.59%); HRA variance 3.42pp (budget 1.07%, actual 2.35%)
findings.quote: Ratio of financing costs to net revenue stream     Non-HRA (8.29%) (4.12%) (8.59%)

findings.paper_title: Appendix A for Treasury Management Annual Report 2025/26
findings.headline: Non-HRA capital expenditure overran budget by £1.4m (9%)
findings.detail: Non-HRA capital spending was £16.565m against a budget of £15.179m, a 9% overspend. Total capital expenditure was £37.549m versus budget of £36.270m. The capital programme exceeded plan, which could indicate delivery challenges or scope changes.
findings.matters: Capital overruns signal execution risk and forecast accuracy issues, affecting the council's ability to deliver planned investment without additional borrowing.
findings.figures: Non-HRA actual £16.565m vs budget £15.179m (£1.386m overspend); total actual £37.549m vs budget £36.270m

findings.headline: Housing revenue account required reserve drawdown for unbudgeted in-year spending pressures
findings.detail: The council drew on HRA reserves during 2025/26 to cover in-year spending pressures, indicating the budget did not fully provide for actual costs. This is a direct and stated reason for the decline in overall liquid reserves available for investment.
findings.matters: Unbudgeted HRA spending pressures suggest either inadequate budgeting or emerging cost pressures in a major service area, both material to council financial management and sustainability
findings.figures: HRA reserve drawdown contributed to overall investment portfolio reduction of approximately £15.2m
findings.quote: This follows on from the outturn position where there was a need to draw on the HRA reserves to fund in-year spending pressures, internal borrowing for Depot project and use of reserves to fund capital expenditure.

findings.headline: Investment portfolio declined sharply as reserves were drawn to fund capital programme and HRA pressures
findings.detail: South Kesteven's investment portfolio fell to an average of £51.260m in Q1 2026/27 from £66.479m in the same period last year. The council drew on reserves during 2025/26 to fund capital expenditure and meet in-year spending pressures in the housing revenue account, directly causing a £415k shortfall against the budgeted investment income of £2.479m.
findings.matters: Declining liquidity and reliance on reserve drawdown to cover expenses budgeted in normal operations weakens the council's financial resilience and raises questions about sustainability
findings.figures: Portfolio average £51.260m vs £66.479m prior year; £415k investment income shortfall against budget of £2.479m
findings.quote: The reduction in the portfolio is largely due to use of reserves to fund the capital programme during the 2025/26 financial year alongside internal borrowing for the depot project in order to avoid incurring external borrowing costs.
